metadata.title: Vernier: Tunable-Precision Certified Abstract Domains for Floating-Point Programs — VMCAI 2027 Artifact
metadata.description:
Self-contained artifact for the VMCAI 2027 paper Vernier: Tunable-Precision Certified Abstract Domains for Floating-Point Programs. A single Docker image bundles the Rust implementation (certkernel), the Lean 4 mechanization of the certificate checkers, and the Apron/ELINA/VPL baselines; no network or repository access is needed at evaluation time.

It reproduces the paper's claims: (C1) float-speed LP with rational soundness and the tunable (k, ℓ) domain family; (C2) an offline-certified fixpoint 8–29× faster than VPL's fastest working configuration; (C3) independently checkable certificates whose checker soundness is mechanized in Lean 4 (soundness theorems resting only on the standard axioms {propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound}, no sorry); and (C4) two genuine soundness bugs the mechanization exposed. Includes smoke.sh, claim-by-claim reproduction scripts, expected outputs, and a reuse/extension guide.

Targets the Available, Functional, and Reusable badges. Third-party baselines (Apron, ELINA, VPL) are included under their own (LGPL) licenses.

metadata.title: Reproducibility Package for Wuming Ternary
metadata.description:
This record contains the frozen computational artifact accompanying the publication Wuming Ternary. It preserves the exact WT 1.0.1 core, guarded wire formats, native modules, CUDA and RTL sources, frozen comparator snapshots, public inputs, deterministic generators, preregistrations, sealed results, statistical procedures, evidence indexes, integrity manifests, and executable release verifiers required to inspect and reconstruct the claims reported in the publication.

Reproduction architecture

The package separates correctness, direct performance, unified-mechanism validation, boundary validation, wire conformance, robustness, and nonidentifiability. Stage 1 supplies the frozen correctness and feasibility gate. Stage 2 uses disjoint entities and executes only after every correctness component has passed.

Each formal experiment retains its own source identity, dependency versions, seeds or public-file hashes, comparator contract, primary endpoint, multiplicity rule, confidence procedure, Stage 1 result, Stage 2 result, and verification entry point. Registered predecessor endpoints are preserved wherever a sealed optimization changed the measured hot path while retaining exact output and the comparison contract.

Data and evidence binding

Generated inputs are reconstructed from frozen scripts and seeds. Public-file experiments use fifteen entity-isolated Canterbury, Large, and pi inputs totaling 15,006,053 bytes. Their source locations, revisions, byte sizes, and SHA-256 digests are recorded in the package.

EVIDENCE_INDEX.json maps the manuscript’s tables and endpoints to their underlying evidence. PAPER_NUMBERS.json is the machine source for reported experimental values. PAPER_ASSERTIONS.json records required manuscript claims and version-chain statements. ENVIRONMENT.json records the original formal execution environment.

The package-internal manifest.json binds the final publication PDF to the paper-number, paper-assertion, and evidence-index files. MANIFEST.sha256 records the SHA-256 digest of every tracked package file. The external manifest.json and WT 1.0.0 Hash.txt bind the final publication PDF and the standalone reproduction-package ZIP.

Verification and execution scope

The root verifier checks all tracked package files, frozen inputs, public-source hashes, current and predecessor version identities, reported paper numbers, evidence indexes, privacy-sensitive paths, and internal release links. The release verifier checks the final delivery filenames, external PDF and ZIP hashes, internal evidence binding, DOCX and PDF numerical parity, OfficeMath requirements, fonts, publication metadata, and selected evidence assertions.

Exact round trips, frame bytes, generated inputs, source hashes, code lengths, rejection counts, statistical rules, evidence indexes, and package integrity can be verified deterministically. Timing values remain hardware dependent. GPU endpoints require a compatible NVIDIA GPU and CUDA environment; CPU verification paths remain available without one.

The package excludes unrelated development trials, caches, credentials, private material, and machine-specific absolute paths. WT-authored code, experiment material, evidence indexes, and documentation are licensed under CC BY-NC-ND 4.0. Third-party software and public corpora remain governed by their original licenses and provenance statements.

Publication concept DOI:
10.5281/zenodo.22084900

Reproduction-package concept DOI:
10.5281/zenodo.22084898

metadata.title: Architecting and Orchestrating Memory-Proximate SIMT Cores: A Quantitative Design Space Exploration for Processing-near-Memory in GPUs
metadata.description:
Artifact for the CODES+ISSS 2026 paper "Architecting and Orchestrating Memory-Proximate SIMT Cores: A Quantitative Design Space Exploration for Processing-near-Memory in GPUs".

The paper evaluates 22 simplified Vortex (RISC-V GPGPU) core configurations for processing-near-memory across 7 memory-proximity scenarios and 24 OpenCL benchmarks, combining ASAP7 7 nm physical design (Yosys + OpenROAD) with cycle-accurate RTL simulation (Verilator), plus KOffE, a per-kernel offloading
framework. This record regenerates every result figure, table and numeric claim in the paper from the raw output of the experimental pipelines.

This artifact contains:

1. pnm-simt-raw-data-and-figures.tar.gz (21 MB)
The raw results and the figure/table scripts, with no toolchain, for checking the published numbers without downloading the image. Needs only Python 3.10+ with numpy and matplotlib. It regenerates every result figure and table in about 3 minutes but cannot re-run the experiments.

tar xzf pnm-simt-raw-data-and-figures.tar.gz
cd pnm-simt-raw-data-and-figures
pip install -r requirements.txt
./scripts/reviewer.sh

2. pnm-simt-artifact-v3.tar.gz (3.1 GB)
The Docker image. It carries the raw results of the experimental pipelines (11,592 Verilator RTL simulation runs, 22 OpenROAD physical-design flows, and the 11,592 SimX runs behind Fig. 10 and the supplementary sweeps), the same figure/table scripts, and the complete toolchain: RISC-V LLVM, PoCL, Verilator, Yosys, OpenROAD and the ASAP7 platform. Docker is the only prerequisite. This is the only route that can re-run the simulations and the physical-design flows.

docker load < pnm-simt-artifact-v3.tar.gz
docker run --rm pnm-simt-codes26-artifact:v3 ./scripts/smoke_test.sh --inner
docker run --rm pnm-simt-codes26-artifact:v3 ./scripts/reviewer.sh

3. CODES'26_S30_AE5_accepted_with_corrections.pdf
The accepted manuscript with post-acceptance corrections applied, highlighted in red. About the corrections: a byte-write-mask defect in the gate-level cache RAM  nstantiation caused a fourfold under-count of data-cache SRAM macros in the accepted version's area and power results. The fix is included here and all physical-design results were re-run with it (baseline: 80,565 um2 / 245 mW to 89,014 um2 / 322 mW). Performance results, configuration rankings, offloading decisions and all qualitative conclusions are unaffected. The camera-ready carries the corrected values, so the manuscript and the regenerated numbers agree. README.md documents this in full.

4. README.md, INSTALL.md, REQUIREMENTS.md, STATUS.md, LICENSE
The documentation. README covers what is regenerated and from which data, the re-run options (--sim N, --phys N, each compared against the shipped values) and the corrections to the accepted paper; INSTALL includes a ~30-second smoke test; REQUIREMENTS lists hardware needs per activity; STATUS states the badges applied for and what the authors have themselves verified; LICENSE is Apache-2.0 with third-party attributions.

5. artifact_part1_reproduce_results.mp4 (1:57)
Demonstration video: regenerating the figures, tables and numeric claims from the shipped raw data, ending in the value-by-value comparison. Every terminal line shown is captured from a real run of this artifact.

6. artifact_part2_rerun_experiments.mp4 (2:47)
Demonstration video: re-running the experimental pipelines themselves, including their measured costs. The full campaigns take days, not minutes; re-running them is not expected for review, and the video shows the supported partial re-runs instead.

Changes in version 3, in response to artifact evaluation feedback: Fig. 10 (KOffE scheduling) is now generated end to end from shipped data. The KOffE analysis resolves its inputs inside the artifact and aborts loudly if they are missing (no fallback of any kind), the plotting script reads only the values the analysis computes (fig10_values.csv, written to out/ by the run), and the final verification now checks seven Fig. 10 values against the paper. The analysis is a seeded, deterministic Monte Carlo, so the figure regenerates identically on every run.
